routes.label: Track the white count and total

question: Initially an urn contains \(100\) black marbles and \(100\) white marbles. Repeatedly, three marbles are removed from the urn and replaced from a pile outside the urn as follows: \[\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Marbles removed} & \text{Replaced with}\\ \hline 3\ \text{black} & 1\ \text{black}\\ \hline 2\ \text{black,}\ 1\ \text{white} & 1\ \text{black,}\ 1\ \text{white}\\ \hline 1\ \text{black,}\ 2\ \text{white} & 2\ \text{white}\\ \hline 3\ \text{white} & 1\ \text{black,}\ 1\ \text{white}\\ \hline\end{array}\] Which of the following sets of marbles could be the contents of the urn after repeated applications of this procedure?
solution:
Track the white marbles because their changes are especially simple. In the first three rules, their number does not change. In the fourth rule, three white marbles are replaced by one white marble, so their number decreases by \(2\). Starting from \(100\), the white count therefore always stays even.

It also stays positive. The only rule that reduces it requires at least three white marbles. Since the count is even, there must then be at least four, leaving at least two afterward. Thus every reachable state contains at least two white marbles. This excludes all the choices except two white marbles.

To prove that this remaining choice can actually occur, continue applying the procedure whenever at least three marbles remain. Some rule always applies, since the four rows cover every possible color combination of three marbles. Each move decreases the total number of marbles by either \(1\) or \(2\), so this process must eventually reach fewer than three marbles.

At that point there are still at least two white marbles. Hence the contents must be exactly \(\boxed{2\text{ white marbles}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
